Kimberly — reviewed the draft. High level feedback and suggested edits for the narrative:

1) Wording: prefer "tenant fencing" over "hardware demarcation" in the auditor narrative; it focuses on the security property rather than implying dedicated physical hardware per tenant.

2) Diagram: the attached topology is good — two small edits: label the control plane endpoints as "Redwood control-plane (multi-tenant, strong auth)" and add an arrow from the customer VPC to the Enclave Gateway showing "customer-managed WG/Transit (optional)".

3) Dedicated pools: we do have NIC-level VLAN tagging for traffic segregation and SR-IOV on the compute hosts when required by contract. Suggest a short sentence: "Dedicated capacity can be configured with host-level affinity and network isolation using VLAN/SR-IOV on supported cloud providers; otherwise, logical tenant fencing is enforced via hypervisor network namespaces and strict ACLs."

4) Evidence bundle: I've added ACL snippets and the KMS trust boundary note into the index (see evidence_index.csv). Also attaching a short plaintext export with the ACL example: 2026-02-17_network-acls-snippets.txt.

Next steps: Rishi — can you confirm the KMS copy and add a line on audit log retention (90 days by default, extendable)? If all good I think we can send to Tina.

- Marissa
Marissa Cole
Principal Cloud Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: small ACL snippet + revised index)

Quick confirm:
- KMS boundary: "Customer keys (BYOK) are stored in customer-managed KMS/HSM when requested for Private deployments. For Dedicated, Redwood can accept customer-managed keys via customer KMS peering or hold keys in our CSP KMS within a dedicated key ring; access is limited to the provisioning service and audited via immutable logs."
- Audit logs: default 90-day retention for token-level traces; SOC/enterprise customers can request 1+ year retention as part of the contract.
- ACL snippets: included in 2026-02-17_network-acls-snippets.txt (egress deny-by-default, explicit host-to-controlplane allow on TCP 443/7022).

I also tightened the diagram caption: "Enclave Gateway mediates control-plane telemetry and dataplane transit without storing customer payloads; tenant KV caches remain scoped to tenant runtime instances."

If no objections, Kimberly — go ahead and send.
